summary: Kazutoshi Soma is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a position as a lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987.
Kazutoshi Ueda (1867–1937) was a linguist and Japanologist who studied under Karl Florenz, whom he later succeeded, and Georg von der Gabelentz. He also founded the Linguistic Society of Japan.

Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies and served as manager at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), and was later a fixed-term assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Shudo High School and the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He founded Shinnyokai, served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989), and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago under Mircea Eliade. Bolle taught at Brown (ca. 1961–1963) and was Professor of History at UCLA (ca. 1969–1996).

Kehan Ding works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and archaeology. Ding earned degrees at Capital University of Economics and Business and the University of Edinburgh (PhD 2018–2024), where Ding served as Course Assistant (2019–2022) and Teaching Fellow (2025).

Kei Kataoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University. He has held appointments at the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, Wolfson College, and Kyushu University as professor (attested 2026).
Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University, where he also serves on the faculty (attested 2026).

Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, completing a doctorate in literature by 1997. He worked at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and was a professor at Kokugakuin University (1995).

Keiji Iwata (1922–2013) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (1944–1947). He later held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (ca. 1967–1980) and Otani University (ca. 1986–1992).
Keiji Kokubu (1907–1997) was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, Nanzan University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and University of Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Hajime Tanabe, and Martin Heidegger. He succeeded Nishida and was a professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964).

Keiki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at and held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2019–2020) and became a visiting scholar at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He founded Miwa Gakuin and taught at Tendai Sect, Shukyo, Taisho, and Tokyo universities.

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held research positions at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).

Keinin Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1998, 2026) and was formerly a lecturer at Waseda University.

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who completed a PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham. He has taught at the University of the Highlands and Islands and served as Senior Lecturer at La Trobe University (2016).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He taught as an associate and visiting professor at Koyasan University and was a professor at Kochi University (ca. 1974–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor at Rissho University, Professor of Indology at Tohoku University (ca. 1980–1993), and president of Hosen Gakuen College (1994–2000).
